documents.text:
Brent Ballard

From:                           Brent Ballard
Sent:                           Tuesday, September 29, 2026 4:02 PM
To:                             ext_Dennis_Moore; ext_Christian_Williams
Cc:                             Justin Poole; Ilka Berrios
Subject:                        Crane Clean Energy Center - Acceptance of Proposed Alternatives VR-01, PR-01, and
                                PR-02 (EPIDs L-2026-LLR-0061, -0062, -0063)


Hi Dennis and Christian,

By letter dated August 27, 2026, as supplemented by letter dated September 17, 2026 (ML26239A016 and
ML26260A184, respectively), Constellation Energy Generation, LLC (the licensee) submitted three alternative
requests for The Christopher M. Crane Clean Energy Center, pursuant to Title 10 of the Code of Federal
Regulations (10 CFR) Section 50.55a(z)(1). This paragraph states Alternatives to the requirements of paragraphs (b)
through (h) of this section or portions thereof may be used when authorized by the Director, O ice of Nuclear
Reactor Regulation. A proposed alternative must be submitted and authorized prior to implementation. The
licensee must demonstrate that the proposed alternative would provide an acceptable level of quality and safety.

The purpose of this email is to provide the results of the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) sta ’s
acceptance review of the licensee’s August 27, 2026, application, as supplemented. The acceptance review was
performed to determine if there is su icient technical information in scope and depth to allow the NRC sta to
complete its detailed technical review. The acceptance review is also intended to identify whether the application
has any readily apparent information insu iciencies in its characterization of the regulatory requirements or the
licensing basis of the plant.

The NRC sta has reviewed the licensee’s application and concluded that it provides technical information in
su icient detail to enable the sta to complete its detailed technical review and make an independent
assessment regarding the acceptability of the proposed requests in terms of regulatory requirements and the
protection of public health and safety and the environment. Given the lesser scope and depth of the acceptance
review, as compared to the detailed technical review, there may be instances in which issues that impact the
sta ’s ability to complete the detailed technical review are identiﬁed despite completion of an adequate
acceptance review. The licensee will be advised of any further information needed to support the sta ’s detailed
technical review by separate correspondence.

Based on the information provided in your submittal, the NRC sta expects to complete its review of the three
applications by February 26, 2027. This estimate is based on the sta ’s initial review of the application, and could
change due to several factors, including requests for additional information. The NRC sta will inform the licensee
of any changes to the estimated completion date.

In accordance with 10 CFR 170.33, which becomes e ective on October 1, 2026, this communication also
establishes a ﬁxed fee cap for the NRC sta to complete its review of the application, as shown below. The NRC
considered various factors when establishing this ﬁxed fee cap, such as the quality and complexity of the
application, technology type, and any pre-application engagement. The Professional Hourly Rate established at 10
CFR 170.20(a) applies to this requested activity.
    - EPID L-2026-LLR-0061, “Proposed Alternative Concerning Testing of the Pressurizer Pilot Operated Relief
        Valve (PORV) in Accordance with 10 CFR 50.55a(z)(1)” (VR-01)
             $32,000.00
    - EPID L-2026-LLR-0062, “Relief Request Concerning Nuclear Services Closed Cooling Water Flow Rate
        Measurement During Group A Tests in Accordance with 10 CFR 50.55a(z)(1)” (PR-01)

                                                         1
            $32,000.00
   -   EPID L-2026-LLR-0063, “Alternative Request to Utilize Code Case OMN-32 Rev 1, ‘Alternative
       Requirements for Range and Accuracy of Pressure, Flow, and Di erential Pressure Instruments Used in
       Pump Tests,’ Proposed Alternative in Accordance with 10 CFR 50.55a(z)(1)” (PR-02)
           $25,000.00

The ﬁxed fee cap represents the maximum amount that the NRC may charge for service fees for the sta ’s review
of the application following acceptance of the complete application. The ﬁxed fee cap will not be increased except
in instances of applicant failure, as deﬁned in 10 CFR 170.3. If applicant failure occurs, the NRC will notify the
licensee in writing of the new ﬁxed fee cap, which will be set at the lowest practicable amount determined by the
NRC to account for the applicant failure and complete the review.

The NRC will track service fees for the application against the ﬁxed fee cap starting today, which is the date a
complete application was accepted for review by the NRC for this requested activity.

Disputes associated with a ﬁxed fee cap must be submitted in accordance with 10 CFR 15.31 and 170.33(f) and
NRC Form 529 procedures. If you have any questions, please contact me.


Brent Ballard
Project Manager
Operating Reactor Licensing Branch 3
Division of Licensing Projects 1
Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation
U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission
